+### DRN-05.04 — The beam, the shield, and the time it takes
+
+**Statement.** Engagement is a fluence model, not hit points: irradiance at the target falls with beam spread and atmospheric loss, so the same emitter needs under a second in close and seconds at reach, and a fine-track lock means a broken beam loses its progress. The shield absorbs first and nothing reaches the airframe until it fails.
+

+
+### DRN-05.05 — Nothing is destroyed in the air
+
+**Statement.** A defeated aircraft is DISABLED and flown down under control to a safe landing. There is no reachable state called destroyed, and a beam on an aircraft already coming down changes nothing about its descent.
+

+|---|---|

+| Vision • 2525 | § I — Humanity First |
+| U-WF trace | `U-WF-06` |
+| R-CORE mode | Manual |
+| De-risk phase | pilot |
+| Declared metric M | every state a beam can reach is one of five, and none of them is destroyed |
+| DTM target | real machines over a real floor with people underneath |
+| Stretch | a physical descent check before every match |
+| Verification | `frontend/tests/drone-laser.test.mjs` |
+| Status | **implemented** |
+
+### DRN-05.06 — Lighting inside the vector law
+
+**Statement.** The engagement reads from stroke colour and weight alone — tracking, absorbing, the moment the shield fails, burning, coming down — plus a shield ring drawn as a declared n-gon that shrinks as the shield is spent. No glow, no gradient, no bloom.
+

+| Status | **implemented** |
+
+### DRN-08.01 — One aircraft, two sizes
+
+**Statement.** The mini foil scales to the full one by geometric similarity, with every derived quantity following the exponent it actually has: area as the square, mass as the cube, stall as the square root. The geometry, the proportions and every rule about materials or people are unchanged by the switch.
+

+| Status | **implemented** |
+
+### DRN-10.06 — The same game at every N
+
+**Statement.** The engagement runs at 1v1, 2v2 and every rung to 21v21 — 42 aircraft, 84 seats — from one model, so what breaks can be found on the way up rather than only at full strength. Each rung is measured for beam waste, contention, decision load and seats.

+### DRN-10.07 — The person is the bottleneck, and it is measured
+
+**Statement.** The invariant that a machine shot needs a named human decision does not bend with N, so the decision load is measured at every rung and compared against what the people present can physically answer. Levels one to three put the decision with one person; four and five put it with a quorum of the key group, which is the only thing that raises a throughput ceiling.

+### DRN-12.01 — From open play to a real floor
+
+**Statement.** Progression runs open play to the winners' circle to a tournament to a physical match. The cut is one ninth, the R-CORE recursion gate, floored and published with its cut line. The score is dominated by accuracy and by whether decisions were answered rather than by kills.

+| Status | **implemented** |

+
+**Statement.** A physical match requires a NAMED safety officer, both crews present, the arena clear of anyone not in the match, and every machine's descent checked. None of those is a score, a perfect record opens none of them, and a refusal names the condition that is missing without discarding the entry.

+### DRN-11.10 — The aircraft is the FOIL
+

The geometry provenance path is the single declared exception, because a derivation that cannot name its source cannot be verified.

+### DRN-07.01 — The address the game answers at
+
+**Statement.** The game is served at /drone-2525 as well as at /main/Drone-2525. Both routes render the one component, their code is identical, and both are emitted to the static export — a route that compiles but does not emit is a 404 in production and green in CI.
